title: Sewing Machine Presser Feet: Which Ones You Really Need
description: Zipper, buttonhole, walking, invisible zip, rolled hem and more: the presser feet worth owning, plus how to check low, high and slant shank before you buy.
h1: The presser feet you really need
intro: The right foot turns a fiddly job into an easy one. Here are the feet worth buying, and how to make sure they fit.

image.alt: Sewing machine presser foot with thread on dark cloth

cardText: The essential feet and how to check shank type.

sections.html: Domestic machines are usually low shank, high shank or slant shank, and many modern machines take snap-on feet on an adaptor. Check the manual before buying.

• Zipper foot: sews close to zip teeth and piping.
  • Buttonhole foot: usually supplied with the machine.
  • Walking foot: feeds layers evenly, ideal for quilting, checks and knits.
  • Invisible zip foot: for concealed zips in dresses and skirts.

• Rolled hem foot for scarves and fine edges.
  • Edge-stitch foot for neat topstitching.
  • Non-stick foot for vinyl and leatherette.
  • Open-toe embroidery foot for appliqué.
